chunks: 8 — Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his father (peace be upon them all). He said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) fell ill with the illness from which he recovered. Fatima the Mistress of Women (peace be upon her) visited him, and with her were al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). She had taken al-Hasan by her right hand and al-Husayn by her left hand, and they walked while Fatima was between them, until they entered the house of A'isha. Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) sat on the right side of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on the left side of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family). They began pressing the part of the Messenger of God's body closest to them, but the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did not awaken from his sleep. So Fatima said to al-Hasan and al-Husayn: 'My beloveds! Your grandfather has dozed off. So, depart for now and leave him until he awakes, then return to him.' They said: 'We are not leaving at this time.' So al-Hasan lay on the right arm of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and al-Husayn on his left arm, and they dozed off. They awoke before the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) awoke, and Fatima (peace be upon her), when they had slept, had returned to her house. So they said to A'isha: 'What did our mother do?' She said: 'When you two fell asleep, she returned to her house.'

So they went out in a dark, pitch-black night of thunder and lightning, and the sky had let loose its rain. A light blazed for them, and they kept walking in that light, al-Hasan gripping with his right hand al-Husayn's left hand, both walking and talking, until they came to the garden of Banu al-Najjar. When they reached the garden they became confused and remained not knowing where to go. Al-Hasan said to al-Husayn: 'We have become confused and remain in this state, not knowing which way to go. So there is no harm in our sleeping at this hour until morning.' Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Go ahead, my brother, do what you see fit.' So they both lay down, each embracing the other, and they slept.

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) then awoke from his sleep and sought them in the house of Fatima, but they were not there. He missed them and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) stood on his feet saying: 'My God, my Master, my Lord! These two are my lion-cubs; they have gone out in hunger and starvation. O God! You are my guardian over them.' A light spread before the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and he continued moving in that light until he reached the garden of Banu al-Najjar, where he found them sleeping, each embracing the other. The sky had cleared above them like a plate, while it was raining as intensely as people had never seen — yet God Almighty had prevented the rain from falling on the spot where they lay sleeping; not a single drop fell on them. They were surrounded by a serpent that had hairs like a thicket of reeds and two wings: one wing covering al-Hasan and one wing covering al-Husayn. When the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) saw them enclosed, he cleared his throat, and the serpent slithered away, saying: 'O God! I call You to witness and Your angels, that these two are the lion-cubs of Your Prophet. I have guarded them and handed them over to him safe and sound.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to it: 'O serpent, who are you?' It said: 'I am the messenger of the jinn to you.' He said: 'Which jinn?' It said: 'The jinn of Nusaybin, a party from Banu Malih. We forgot a verse of the Book of God Almighty, so they sent me to you so that you might teach us what we have forgotten of the Book of God. When I reached this place, I heard a caller calling: O serpent! These two are the lion-cubs of the Messenger of God, so guard them from afflictions, ailments, and the calamities of night and day. So I guarded them and have handed them over to you safe and sound.' The serpent then took the verse and departed.

Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) took al-Hasan and placed him on his right shoulder, and placed al-Husayn on his left shoulder. Ali (peace be upon him) came out and joined the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family). One of his companions said to him: 'May my father and mother be your ransom — hand one of your two cubs to me so I may lighten your load.' He said: 'Go on — God has heard your words and knows your station.' Another met him and said: 'May my father and mother be your ransom — hand one of your two cubs to me so I may lighten your load.' He said: 'Go on — God has heard your words and knows your station.' Then Ali (peace be upon him) met him and said: 'May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of God — hand me one of my two cubs and your two cubs so I may lighten your load.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) turned to al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Hasan, would you go to your father's shoulder?' He replied: 'By God, O dear grandfather, your shoulder is more beloved to me than my father's.' Then he turned to al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Husayn, would you go to your father's shoulder?' He replied: 'By God, O dear grandfather, I say to you what my brother al-Hasan said — your shoulder is more beloved to me than my father's.' So he brought them both to Fatima's home (peace be upon her), and she had saved some dates for them. She placed them before the two of them, and they ate and were satisfied and rejoiced. Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to them: 'Now get up and wrestle.' They got up to wrestle. Fatima (peace be upon her) had gone out for some errand and then entered, and she heard the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) saying: 'Come on, O Hasan — press on al-Husayn and throw him down!' She said to him: 'O father, how strange! Are you encouraging this one against that one — are you encouraging the elder against the younger?' He said to her: 'O my dear daughter, are you not content that I say: O Hasan, press on al-Husayn and throw him down — while my beloved Jibril is saying: O Husayn, press on al-Hasan and throw him down!?'

key_terms.الْمَخْمَصَةُ وَالْمَجَاعَةُ: Hunger and starvation — indicating the poverty of the Prophet's household
key_terms.جِنُّ نَصِيبِينَ: Jinn of Nusaybin — a group of jinn from the city of Nusaybin (Nisibis) who sought Quranic instruction from the Prophet
key_terms.سَيِّدَةُ النِّسَاءِ: Mistress of Women — an honorific title for Fatima al-Zahra (AS)
key_terms.شِبْلَايَ: My two lion-cubs — an affectionate title used by the Prophet for al-Hasan and al-Husayn
key_terms.عَزَالِي: Rain-pouches of the sky — poetic expression for heavy rainfall

ai.seo_question: What is the story of al-Hasan and al-Husayn getting lost and protected by a jinn serpent during the Prophet's illness?
ai.summary: This narrative from al-Amali of al-Saduq, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq back to Imam al-Sajjad, recounts the miraculous night of al-Hasan and al-Husayn during the Prophet's illness. When the two grandsons became lost in a dark stormy night while returning to their mother Fatima, God sent a miraculous light to guide them and dispatched a jinn serpent to protect them. The hadith highlights the special divine protection accorded to the Ahlulbayt, the love of the grandsons for their grandfather, and ends with the charming detail of Gabriel encouraging al-Husayn in wrestling while the Prophet cheered al-Hasan.
